statement: Ògún is consistently sourced as patron of iron-working, hunting, and war from an early period, with the domain demonstrably expanding over time to cover new iron/steel-adjacent technologies. Sandra T. Barnes, ed., Africa's Ogun: Old World and New (Indiana UP, 1989/1997), the standard interdisciplinary scholarly volume, is explicitly organized around this transformation-across-manifestations thesis. A popular (non-academic) claim that Ògún was a historicized Ifè king could not be verified against any academic source in this research pass — contrast with Ṣàngó, whose historicization is well-attested in named academic literature; do not report the Ògún claim with comparable confidence.

sources.citation: Barnes, Sandra T., ed. Africa's Ogun: Old World and New. Indiana University Press, 1989/2nd ed. 1997.

does_not_demonstrate: That Ògún was a historicized Ifè king — a popular, non-academically-sourced claim distinct from Ṣàngó's well-attested historicization case
